The institution said no student was shot or killed on its campus, contrary to claims that a student identified as Ayo, popularly known as Jackson, an ND I Art student, died during the alleged incident on Friday, November 13, 2026.
Reports emerged on social media that a student identified simply as Ayo had been killed after allegedly making advances towards a woman suspected to be the girlfriend of a cult leader on campus.
A post by an X (formerly Twitter user identified as “Chameleon” described the deceased as her cousin and claimed Ayo, reportedly a National Diploma (ND) 1 student, was shot in the chest.
“My cousin was shot in the chest at YABATECH yesterday over a woman. Life is truly unfair. May your soul continue to rest in perfect peace, Ayo,” the user wrote.
Reports alleged that Ayo had been pursuing a romantic relationship with the woman, said to be an ND 2 student.
According to the post on X, It was gathered that the cult leader, angered by Ayo’s advances towards his girlfriend, cornered him outside the school gate and shot him at least twice
The College’s position was contained in an official statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Adekunle Adams, who urged students, parents, guardians and members of the public to disregard the report.
However, the statement said students were writing their examinations on the day of the alleged incident, adding that the ongoing examination exercise remained peaceful, with no security breach of the nature being circulated.
The institution debunk the reports as Fake News as it also reaffirmed its zero-tolerance policy on cultism and other social vices, stressing that it had strengthened its security arrangements in collaboration with relevant state security agencies to safeguard lives and property within the campus.
It said the security measures included intelligence-driven mechanisms aimed at preventing, detecting and addressing potential threats to the safety of students and staff.
The College further stated that it supported the lawful arrest and prosecution of anyone found engaging in cult-related activities.
On efforts to prevent cultism, YABATECH said it regularly organised sensitisation programmes, symposia, guidance and counselling sessions to discourage students from engaging in cult-related activities and other anti-social behaviours.
It, however, cautioned social media users and other information disseminators against circulating unverified reports capable of causing unnecessary panic and damaging the institution’s reputation.
The statement urged stakeholders to verify information from appropriate authorities before publishing or sharing it, adding that the institution remained committed to providing a safe, peaceful and conducive environment for teaching, learning and research.
